findings.title: Unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when no TopicUser row exists
findings.body: `TopicUser.find_by(user_id:, topic_id:)` returns nil when the user has no topic_users row for the topic. That happens, for example, to a user who was mentioned or quoted in a topic they never visited. The next line calls `tu.notification_level` on nil, so clicking the email unsubscribe link raises NoMethodError and returns a 500. Use `TopicUser.change`, which creates the row if needed, or handle the nil case explicitly.

findings.title: save! bypasses TopicUser.change, so the level can be silently reverted and clients are not notified
findings.body: The level is written with `tu.save!` instead of `TopicUser.change`. As a result `notifications_reason_id` and `notifications_changed_at` are not set, and no MessageBus `notification_level_change` is published to the user's open clients. When `notifications_reason_id` is still NULL, `update_last_read` auto-promotes the row back to `tracking` once read time exceeds the auto-track threshold. A user who unsubscribed can therefore be re-subscribed just by reading the topic. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user, topic_id, notification_level: ...)`.

findings.title: State-changing unsubscribe exposed as a GET with no CSRF protection, and it toggles on repeat
findings.body: The unsubscribe action changes the user's notification level on a plain GET. Any third-party page can embed `` and change a logged-in user's settings. Email link scanners, prefetchers and page reloads also trigger it. The action is not idempotent: the first hit drops watching/tracking to regular, and a second hit (a refresh or revisit) drops regular to muted. The user ends up muted without intending it. Have the GET render a confirmation page and perform the change via POST/PUT, or use a signed per-user token.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link now needs %{unsubscribe_url}; senders that don't pass it break
findings.body: The shared `unsubscribe_link` string now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `MessageBuilder#body` and `#html_part` render it for every email built with `add_unsubscribe_link: true`. Only `send_notification_email` was updated to pass `unsubscribe_url`. Any other sender that sets `add_unsubscribe_link` without it will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument or render a broken link. Even when the URL is present, the per-topic sentence is wrong for emails that are not about a single topic. Use a separate translation key, or only add the topic sentence when `unsubscribe_url` is present.

findings.title: No tests for the new unsubscribe endpoint
findings.body: The new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action has no controller specs. Untested cases include the level transitions (watching/tracking to regular, regular to muted), the missing-TopicUser case, the slug redirect, and the logged-out behavior. The only spec change adds an `unsubscribe_url` argument to an existing MessageBuilder test and does not assert that the link appears.
